question: How do we make the top customers endpoint fast?
context: GET /stats/top-customers ranks customers by paid revenue over the last 30 days. It scans about 200,000 orders on every call and is slow under load. The sales dashboard polls it, and account managers use it right after closing large orders, so results must not lag far behind new orders.

baseline.name: Today (no change)
baseline.description: The code as it is now.

options.name: Cache
options.description: Cache the endpoint's response in memory with a 60 second time to live.

options.name: Materialized view
options.description: Precompute the ranking in a Postgres materialized view and refresh it in the background every 5 seconds.

options.name: Index and rewrite
options.description: Add the right index or indexes and rewrite the query so Postgres does less work. No caching and no precomputed tables.

diff.patch:
diff --git a/demo/orders-api/src/db.ts b/demo/orders-api/src/db.ts
index fa3c0a9..ca573ef 100644
--- a/demo/orders-api/src/db.ts
+++ b/demo/orders-api/src/db.ts
@@ -23,4 +23,12 @@ export async function openDb(): Promise<PGlite> {
     );
 
+    -- Covering index for the top-customers query:
+    --   equality on status, range on created_at (newest first),
+    --   INCLUDE avoids heap fetches for customer_id and amount_cents
+    --   so the aggregate can be satisfied by an index-only scan.
+    CREATE INDEX orders_status_created_covering
+      ON orders (status, created_at DESC)
+      INCLUDE (customer_id, amount_cents);
+
     SELECT setseed(0.42);
 
diff --git a/demo/orders-api/src/server.ts b/demo/orders-api/src/server.ts
index a612221..6dacad6 100644
--- a/demo/orders-api/src/server.ts
+++ b/demo/orders-api/src/server.ts
@@ -13,15 +13,26 @@ export interface TopCustomer {
 export async function topCustomers(db: PGlite, limit: number): Promise<TopCustomer[]> {
   const { rows } = await db.query<TopCustomer>(
-    `SELECT c.id AS customer_id,
+    // Aggregate on orders first (index-only scan on orders_status_created_covering),
+    // then join the small aggregated set to customers for the name.
+    // This lets Postgres resolve the GROUP BY entirely from the index and only
+    // touch the customers table for at most LIMIT rows.
+    `WITH ranked AS (
+       SELECT o.customer_id,
+              sum(o.amount_cents)::int AS revenue_cents,
+              count(*)::int           AS orders
+       FROM   orders o
+       WHERE  o.status     = 'paid'
+         AND  o.created_at > now() - interval '30 days'
+       GROUP  BY o.customer_id
+       ORDER  BY revenue_cents DESC
+       LIMIT  $1
+     )
+     SELECT r.customer_id,
             c.name,
-            sum(o.amount_cents)::int AS revenue_cents,
-            count(*)::int AS orders
-     FROM orders o
-     JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
-     WHERE o.status = 'paid'
-       AND o.created_at > now() - interval '30 days'
-     GROUP BY c.id, c.name
-     ORDER BY revenue_cents DESC
-     LIMIT $1`,
+            r.revenue_cents,
+            r.orders
+     FROM   ranked r
+     JOIN   customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id
+     ORDER  BY r.revenue_cents DESC`,
     [limit],
   );

verdict.headline: No option meets every constraint.
verdict.reason: Closest is Index and rewrite, which misses p95 latency. Relax a constraint or add an option.
